DJ1.claim: Darjeeling, at about 2,045 m, became a British hill station after Sikkim ceded it to the East India Company in 1835, and later the summer capital of the Bengal Presidency.

evidence.quote: Elevation [ b ] 2,045 m (6,709 ft)
Before the East India Company took over in 1835, Darjeeling was part of Sikkim.
Thus, Darjeeling came under British control and became the summer capital of the Bengal Presidency.

DJ2.claim: Darjeeling became home to thousands of Tibetans who followed the Dalai Lama into exile after 1959.

evidence.quote: became home to thousands of Tibetans who followed the Dalai Lama to take refuge in India after the Tibetan uprising in 1959.

DJ3.claim: Bagdogra airport is about 90 km away; by road, Darjeeling is 77 km from Siliguri on NH 110. The toy train starts at New Jalpaiguri.

evidence.quote: The nearest airport is Bagdogra Airport , located 90 km (56 mi) from Darjeeling.
Darjeeling can be reached by motorized vehicles on National Highway 110, from Siliguri, 77 km (48 mi) away.

DJ4.claim: About 80% of Darjeeling's rain falls from June to September, when landslides often disrupt road and rail links.

evidence.quote: Eighty percent of the annual rainfall takes place between the months of June and September
However, road and railway communications often get disrupted in the monsoons because of landslides.

DJ5.claim: October to November offers the clearest mountain views; April to June is also pleasant.

evidence.quote: October to November offers the clearest views
The best time to visit Observatory Hill is from April to June, when the weather is pleasant and clear for panoramic views of the mountains and Darjeeling.

DJ6.claim: Try momos, thukpa, sha phaley, sel roti and butter tea — Darjeeling's food blends Nepali, Sikkimese, Tibetan and Bengali traditions.

evidence.quote: the culinary cultures that rule Darjeeling are varied, ranging from Nepali and Sikkimese to Tibetan and of course, Bengali.
Savour the sweet delights of Sel Roti, deep-fried rice doughnuts served with butter or chutney
And don't miss the hearty Thukpa, a hot noodle soup brimming with meat, vegetables, and spices

DJ7.claim: Glenary's bakery and café dates from 1888; Keventer's is a colonial-era breakfast institution.

evidence.quote: This iconic bakery and café, established in 1888, serves delectable pastries
Start your day at Keventer's, a charming colonial-era establishment known for its scrumptious breakfast options.

DJ8.claim: Look for Darjeeling tea, the Gorkha khukuri knife, thangka paintings, singing bowls and prayer flags.

evidence.quote: discover the significance of the Khukuri, a sharp and curved knife that symbolises the pride and bravery of the Gorkha community.
Don't miss the opportunity to shop for Tibetan souvenirs, including enchanting artefacts like singing bowls, prayer wheels, prayer flags, Thangkas (Tibetan wall paintings)

DJ9.claim: The Darjeeling Carnival runs for 10 days in November, Losar (Tibetan New Year) falls in February–March, and Buddha Jayanti in May.

evidence.quote: the 10-day Darjeeling Carnival in November
In February and March, the vibrant Tibetan New Year, Losha
Finally, in May, Buddha Jayanti finds Buddhist temples adorned in celebration

DJ10.claim: The Himalayan Mountaineering Institute, founded in 1954 after the first ascent of Everest, has a museum of expedition gear and photographs, with Tenzing Norgay's memorial outside.

evidence.quote: was established in Darjeeling , India on 4 November 1954
The institute has exhibits of equipment, photographs and stories about Edmund Hillary, Tenzing Norgay and various other mountaineers.
Just outside the museum is the statue of Tenzing Norgay where his remains are also kept.

DJ11.claim: The Tibetan Refugee Self Help Centre, founded in 1959, has workshops where you can watch carpets and thangkas being made.

evidence.quote: Founded in 1959, this centre honours the courage of the Tibetan people who fled to India during political unrest.
Watch as skilled craftsmen and women create beautiful handcrafted items such as carpets, thangka paintings, and traditional Tibetan handicrafts.

DJ12.claim: Monasteries include Yiga Choling (built 1850) at Ghum; the white Japanese Peace Pagoda was built by Nipponzan Myohoji.

evidence.quote: Yiga Choling gompa, one of the oldest monasteries in this region built in 1850
Built by the Japanese Buddhist Nipponzan Myohoji organization, the large white pagoda has numerous carvings of Buddha and his preaching.

DJ13.claim: The Mall and Chowrasta are the town's social heart — best in the evening.

evidence.quote: An ideal time to explore the famous mall road of Darjeeling is in the evening.

DJ_112.claim: 112 is India's single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance.

evidence.quote: 112 is now the pan-country single emergency number for all emergencies.

DJ_VISA.claim: e-Tourist visa applications should be made at least 4 days before arrival, with a passport valid for at least six months.

evidence.quote: For e-Tourist and e-Business visa, Applicants of the eligible countries/territories may apply online minimum 4 days in advance of the date of arrival.
Applicant's passport should have at least six months validity at the time of making application for grant of e-Visa.

DJ_UPI.claim: International visitors can pay by QR code using NPCI's UPI One World wallet after a passport-and-visa KYC check.

evidence.quote: The UPI One World wallet can be availed through authorized PPI issuers at airports, hotels, designated money exchange locations and other touchpoints, following a full KYC process based on a passport and valid visa.

DH1.claim: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999, later part of the Mountain Railways of India.

evidence.quote: On 5 December 1999, UNESCO declared the DHR a World Heritage Site .
the site became known as one of the mountain railways of India

DH2.claim: Built between 1879 and 1881, the 2-ft-gauge line runs about 88 km from New Jalpaiguri to Darjeeling, climbing from about 100 m to 2,200 m with six zig-zags and three loops.

evidence.quote: Built between 1879 and 1881, it is about 88 km (55 mi) long.
It climbs from about 100 m (330 ft) above sea level at New Jalpaiguri to about 2,200 m (7,200 ft) at Darjeeling, using six zig zags and three loops (originally five) to gain altitude.

DH3.claim: Ghum station sits at 2,260 m; at Batasia Loop (1919), 5 km from Darjeeling, the track spirals around a hill beside the Gorkha War Memorial.

evidence.quote: Ghum station is situated at an altitude of 2,260 metres (7,410 ft) .
At this point, the track spirals around over itself from the bottom of a small hill and over the hilltop. It was commissioned in 1919.
It is 5 km (3 mi) from Darjeeling, below Ghum .

DH4.claim: Vintage B-class steam locomotives still haul special services; Mark Twain rode the line in 1895.

evidence.quote: Steam-enthusiast specials are hauled by vintage British-built B-Class steam locomotives .
Mark Twain, the renowned American writer, rode this Toy Train in 1895.

TH1.claim: Tiger Hill (2,590 m) is famous for sunrise views of Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest peak, with Everest visible beyond.

evidence.quote: at an elevation of 8,482 feet (2,590 meters) offers an unparalleled view of the world’s highest peaks, including Mount Everest and Mount Kanchenjunga.
Kanchenjunga, the world’s third-highest peak, dominates the scene.

TH2.claim: In peak season crowds and traffic jams are common; Incredible India suggests arriving around 3:30 am.

evidence.quote: in peak season, there is always a throng of people making their way up – and traffic jams are not uncommon. Arrive early, around 3:30 am, to secure a spot.

TH3.claim: Stop at Batasia Loop, Ghum Monastery and the Senchal Wildlife Sanctuary on the way down.

evidence.quote: On the way back from Tiger Hill, you can stop by Batasia Loop, Ghum Monastery and the Senchal Wildlife Sanctuary.

TH4.claim: Everest and Kanchenjunga, both visible from Tiger Hill, are 172 km apart; the hilltop gives a 360-degree panorama.

evidence.quote: The distance between them—172 kilometres (107 miles)—adds to Everest’s mystique.
Tiger Hill provides a 360-degree panorama that stretches from the snow-capped Himalayas to the lush green valleys below.

HV1.claim: Happy Valley Tea Estate, founded in 1854, sits at about 2,100 m and covers 177 hectares; some bushes are 150 years old.

evidence.quote: The Happy Valley Tea Estate was founded in 1854
The tea estate is situated at a height of 2,100 meters (6,900 feet) and spans 177 hectares (440 acres).
some of them are 150 years old

HV2.claim: Visitors can see leaves withered, rolled, oxidised and dried in the factory, then taste first- and second-flush teas.

evidence.quote: Observe how the tea leaves are dried, oxidised, rolled, and withered
from delicate first-flush brews to strong second-flush brews

HV3.claim: Incredible India lists opening hours of 8 am to 4:30 pm.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 08:00 AM
Closing time - 04:30 PM

HV4.claim: Leaves are still harvested by hand.

evidence.quote: Witness the expert labourers as they skillfully harvest the delicate tea leaves by hand

HV5.claim: The estate was first planted with bushes imported from China; walks lead over the surrounding hillsides.

evidence.quote: The estate was initially established with tea bushes imported from China
Take leisurely walks along the hillsides surrounding the area

ZO1.claim: Established in 1958 at about 7,000 ft, the zoo is known for conservation breeding of red pandas, snow leopards and the Tibetan wolf.

evidence.quote: Established in 1958
situated on 7000ft above the sea level
internationally recognised for its conservation breeding programmes of Red Panda, Snow Leopards, Tibetan Wolf

ZO2.claim: Incredible India lists 8:30 am–4:30 pm in summer and 8:30 am–4 pm in winter.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 08:30 AM to 04:30 PM (Summers)
08:30 AM to 04:00 PM (Winters)

ZO3.claim: It is a 20–30 minute downhill walk from Chowrasta.

evidence.quote: Conveniently located a mere 20 to 30 minute downhill walk from Chowrasta Mall Road

ZO4.claim: Residents include snow leopards, clouded leopards, Himalayan black bears, red pandas, blue sheep and Himalayan tahr.

evidence.quote: Among its celebrated residents are the elusive snow leopard, the majestic Himalayan wolf, clouded leopard, Himalayan black bear, Himalayan deer and the charming red panda

ZO5.claim: The zoo is named after Padmaja Naidu, daughter of Sarojini Naidu, and has a large circular aviary.

evidence.quote: Named in honour of Padmaja Naidu, the daughter of Sarojini Naidu
The zoo also has an Aviary, a huge circular bird's cage

OB2.claim: One suggestion traces Darjeeling's name to this hill — either to the Shiva shrine or to the Bhutia Busty monastery that once stood here.

evidence.quote: It has interestingly been suggested that the very name “Darjeeling” might trace its origins to this sacred spot.
since Observatory Hill was the original location of the Bhutia Busty Gompa

OB1.claim: Observatory Hill, above Chowrasta, has the Mahakal Temple and views of Kanchenjunga on clear days.

evidence.quote: Perched atop Observatory Hill, the Mahakal Temple stands as a beacon of spiritual devotion.
Rising above Chowrasta square or the Mall as it is popularly known in Darjeeling, Observatory Hill is an elevated vantage point that offers breathtaking views of snow-clad peaks

SD1.claim: Sandakphu (3,636 m) on the Singalila Ridge, on the Nepal border, is West Bengal's highest point, with views of Everest, Lhotse, Makalu and Kanchenjunga.

evidence.quote: Located at an impressive height of 3,636 meters, Sandakphu sits atop the Singalila Ridge in the Darjeeling district, marking the peaceful border with Nepal.
including Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, and the revered Kanchenjunga

SD2.claim: Treks start at Manebhanjan, about 28 km (roughly an hour by road) from Darjeeling, and pass through Singalila National Park in stages via Chitre and Meghma.

evidence.quote: Treks begin at Manebhanjan which is 28 km (17 mi) (approx. 1 hour by road) from Darjeeling .
The Sandakphu trekking routes inside the Singalila National Park have four legs or stages.
Manebhanjan to Meghma – height 2,600 m (8,500 ft) : This is a 4-hour trek through the lower forest. The route goes via Chitre.

SD3.claim: Rhododendrons and orchids bloom in spring, and the red panda lives in the surrounding forests.

evidence.quote: particularly the uncommon and unique rhododendrons and orchids that add bright colours to the scenery during springtime
The elusive red panda also resides in this sanctuary

SD4.claim: From Sandakphu, a one-day, 21-km trek continues to Phalut.

evidence.quote: Sandakphu to Phalut – height 3,600 m (11,800 ft) : It is a one-day trek via Sabarkum – height 3,536 m (11,601 ft) covering 21 km (13 mi) .

places.name: Darjeeling
places.summary: The Queen of the Hills: Kanchenjunga sunrises from Tiger Hill, the UNESCO toy train, tea estates, monasteries and momos.
places.seoTitle: Darjeeling Travel Guide: Toy Train, Tiger Hill & Tea
places.seoDescription: Plan a Darjeeling trip: the UNESCO toy train, sunrise at Tiger Hill, Happy Valley tea estate, the zoo and HMI, monasteries, food and the best time to visit.

images.commons: File:Mount Kangchenjunga seen from Tiger Hill.jpg
images.alt: The snow-covered Kanchenjunga range above forested ridges and the town of Darjeeling under a blue sky
images.caption: Kanchenjunga from Tiger Hill, Darjeeling

overview.text:
Darjeeling sits at about 2,045 m in the hills of northern West Bengal, facing Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest mountain. Sikkim ceded it to the East India Company in 1835, and it grew into a hill station and the summer capital of the Bengal Presidency. After 1959, thousands of Tibetans settled here, and their monasteries and crafts are part of the town's character.

Ride the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, a UNESCO World Heritage Site; rise before dawn for the sunrise from Tiger Hill; and tour a tea estate such as Happy Valley, founded in 1854. The Himalayan Mountaineering Institute tells the story of Everest climbers, and for trekkers, Sandakphu on the Nepal border is West Bengal's highest point.

best_time.text: October to November brings the clearest mountain views, and April to June is pleasant too. About 80% of Darjeeling's rain falls between June and September, when landslides often disrupt road and rail links.

how_to_reach.text: The nearest airport is Bagdogra, about 90 km away. By road, Darjeeling is 77 km from Siliguri on NH 110. The toy train runs 88 km from New Jalpaiguri, the main railhead.

items.body: Momos, thukpa and sha phaley from Tibetan kitchens.
Sel roti, a sweet rice-flour ring, and Nepali thalis.
Breakfast at Keventer's and cakes at Glenary's, founded in 1888.
Darjeeling tea, fresh from the estates.
Watch sunrise over Kanchenjunga from Tiger Hill.
Ride the toy train to Ghum and Batasia Loop.
Tour Happy Valley Tea Estate and taste first- and second-flush teas.
See red pandas and snow leopards at the zoo, and the mountaineering museum at HMI.
Watch carpet weavers at the Tibetan Refugee Self Help Centre.
Visit Yiga Choling monastery and the Japanese Peace Pagoda.
Shop for khukuris, thangkas and singing bowls; stroll the Mall in the evening.

items.title: Visas
items.body: Apply for an e-Tourist visa at least 4 days before arrival; your passport needs at least six months' validity.

items.title: Payments
items.body: Visitors can pay by QR code with NPCI's UPI One World wallet after a passport-and-visa KYC check. Carry some cash for small purchases.

items.title: Emergency
items.body: Dial 112 for police, fire or ambulance.
Bring warm layers for Tiger Hill — it is cold before dawn.
Plan around the Darjeeling Carnival in November or Losar in February–March for festivals.

places.name: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway
places.summary: The UNESCO-listed 'toy train', climbing 88 km from the plains to Darjeeling through loops and zig-zags.
places.seoTitle: Darjeeling Toy Train: Route, Batasia Loop & Tips
places.seoDescription: Ride the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway: its UNESCO-listed history, the 88 km route from New Jalpaiguri, Ghum, Batasia Loop and steam specials.

images.alt: A small blue steam locomotive and carriages of the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway on Batasia Loop
images.caption: Steam train on Batasia Loop

overview.text:
The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway — the 'toy train' — was built between 1879 and 1881. The 2-ft-gauge line runs about 88 km from New Jalpaiguri to Darjeeling, climbing from about 100 m to 2,200 m with six zig-zags and three loops. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999, and is now part of the Mountain Railways of India.

The highest station, Ghum, sits at 2,260 m. Just below it, at Batasia Loop (1919), the track spirals around a hill beside the Gorkha War Memorial. Vintage B-class steam locomotives still haul special services, and Mark Twain rode the line in 1895.

items.body: Check current schedules and book seats ahead, especially in peak season.
The short ride from Darjeeling to Ghum and Batasia Loop is a good taste of the line.

places.name: Tiger Hill
places.summary: Darjeeling's famous sunrise viewpoint over Kanchenjunga and Everest.
places.seoTitle: Tiger Hill Sunrise, Darjeeling: Timing & Tips
places.seoDescription: Watch sunrise from Tiger Hill near Darjeeling: views of Kanchenjunga and Everest, when to arrive, crowds and stops on the way back.

images.alt: The snow-covered summit of Kanchenjunga against a pale blue morning sky
images.caption: Kanchenjunga from Tiger Hill

overview.text: Tiger Hill rises to 2,590 m south of Darjeeling and is famous for its sunrise. As the first light reaches the peaks, Kanchenjunga — the world's third-highest mountain — turns gold, and on clear mornings Everest is visible beyond it. In peak season the road up is crowded and traffic jams are common, so Incredible India suggests arriving around 3:30 am. On the way back, stop at Batasia Loop, Ghum Monastery and the Senchal Wildlife Sanctuary.

items.body: Kanchenjunga, the world's third-highest peak, catching the first light.
Everest on the horizon — 172 km beyond Kanchenjunga.
A 360-degree panorama from the snow peaks to the valleys below.
Bring warm layers and a flask of tea — it is cold before dawn.
October to November usually gives the clearest skies.

places.name: Happy Valley Tea Estate

places.seoTitle: Happy Valley Tea Estate, Darjeeling: Tours & Timings
places.seoDescription: Visit Happy Valley Tea Estate in Darjeeling: its 1854 history, how tea is made, tasting first- and second-flush teas, and opening hours.

images.commons: File:Happy Valley Tea Estate, Darjeeling, India.jpg
images.alt: Terraced green tea bushes on a misty hillside at Happy Valley Tea Estate, Darjeeling
images.caption: Happy Valley Tea Estate

overview.text: Founded in 1854, Happy Valley Tea Estate covers 177 hectares of hillside at about 2,100 m, just below the town. Some of its bushes are 150 years old, and the leaves are still picked by hand. In the factory you can follow the leaves as they are withered, rolled, oxidised and dried, then compare delicate first-flush teas with stronger second-flush ones in the tasting room. Afterwards, paths lead out over the surrounding hillsides for a leisurely walk among the tea bushes.

items.body: Pickers harvesting leaves by hand on the slopes.
The factory, where leaves are withered, rolled, oxidised and dried.
A tasting of first- and second-flush teas.
Walks over the hillsides around the estate, first planted with bushes from China.

items.title: Opening hours
items.body: 8 am – 4:30 pm (Incredible India listing).

places.summary: A high-altitude zoo known for breeding red pandas and snow leopards, with the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute next door.
places.seoTitle: Darjeeling Zoo & HMI: Red Pandas, Timings & Tips
places.seoDescription: Visit the Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park and the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute in Darjeeling: animals, conservation breeding and opening hours.

images.commons: File:Red Panda, Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park, Darjeeling.jpg
images.alt: A red panda curled up asleep on a tree branch
images.caption: Red panda, Darjeeling zoo

overview.text:
Established in 1958 at about 7,000 ft, Darjeeling's zoo is known for its conservation breeding of red pandas, snow leopards and the Tibetan wolf. Other residents include clouded leopards, Himalayan black bears, blue sheep and Himalayan tahr. It is a 20–30 minute downhill walk from Chowrasta.

The Himalayan Mountaineering Institute, founded in 1954 after the first ascent of Everest, shares the hillside. Its museum displays equipment, photographs and stories of Tenzing Norgay, Edmund Hillary and other climbers, and Tenzing's memorial stands outside.

items.body: Red pandas and snow leopards, the stars of its breeding programmes.
A large circular aviary of pheasants, parakeets and mynas.
The HMI museum of Everest expeditions.

items.title: Opening hours
items.body: 8:30 am – 4:30 pm (summer); 8:30 am – 4 pm (winter), per Incredible India.

places.name: Observatory Hill
places.summary: The hill above Chowrasta with the Mahakal Temple and views of Kanchenjunga.
places.seoDescription: Observatory Hill in Darjeeling: the Mahakal Temple and mountain views.

overview.text: Rising above Chowrasta and the Mall, Observatory Hill is crowned by the Mahakal Temple, dedicated to Shiva and draped in prayer flags. On clear days it offers views of Kanchenjunga; October to November usually brings the clearest skies. One theory traces the name Darjeeling to this hill.

places.name: Sandakphu
places.summary: West Bengal's highest point (3,636 m) on the Singalila Ridge, with views of four of the world's five highest peaks.
places.seoTitle: Sandakphu Trek: Route, Best Season & Views
places.seoDescription: Plan the Sandakphu trek from Darjeeling: the route from Manebhanjan through Singalila National Park, the views of Everest and Kanchenjunga, and the best season.

images.commons: File:Kangchenjunga (Kanchenjunga) from Singalila National Park, Sandakphu.jpg
images.alt: The Kanchenjunga massif glowing under pink clouds above blue ridges, seen from Sandakphu
images.caption: Kanchenjunga from Sandakphu

overview.text:
Sandakphu, at 3,636 m on the Singalila Ridge along the Nepal border, is the highest point in West Bengal. From the top you can see Everest, Lhotse, Makalu and Kanchenjunga — the 'Sleeping Buddha'.

Treks start at Manebhanjan, about 28 km (roughly an hour by road) from Darjeeling, and climb through Singalila National Park in stages: the first leg to Meghma, via Chitre, takes about four hours through the lower forest. From Sandakphu, a further one-day, 21-km trek leads to Phalut. In spring the ridge is bright with rhododendrons and orchids, and red pandas live in the forest.

items.body: Arrange permits, guides and teahouse stays through a registered local operator — check current rules before you go.
Pack for freezing nights, even outside winter.
